consumer_seed: The Connected Nations Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
The update is a snapshot of mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
The update is an interim update to Connected Nations 2025, which used July 2025 data.
The fixed-broadband section covers fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access network availability.
The update reports full-fibre take-up in addition to availability.
The report uses at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload for decent broadband.
Mobile coverage reporting uses signal-strength predictions from the four mobile network operators.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises as of January 2026.
The 24.9 million full-fibre figure represented 82% of the UK's 30.5 million homes.
Full-fibre availability increased by 1.2 million homes in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million connections across residential and commercial premises.
The 12.4 million full-fibre connections represented 47% of premises with access to full fibre.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 89%, or 27.1 million homes.
The report estimated 4,000 premises without access to affordable decent broadband.
The Planned Network Deployments 2026 report was published on 13 May 2026.
The report examines anticipated full-fibre and gigabit-capable coverage by the end of 2028.
The deployment plans were stated by network operators as of January 2026.
The report covers operator plans over the following three years.
The plans include privately funded deployments and plans supported through public funds or intervention.
The report does not separately count rollout aspirations or plans of public authorities.
If all plans are realised, full fibre could be available to 28.1 million UK homes by the end of 2028.
The 28.1 million projection represents 92% of residential properties.
The report uses a January 2026 full-fibre baseline of 24.9 million homes, or 82%.
If all plans are realised, gigabit-capable coverage could reach 29 million homes.
The 29 million projection represents 95% gigabit-capable coverage.
All-plan full-fibre coverage by January 2028 was projected at 90%.
High Confidence plans alone could produce 87% full-fibre coverage by January 2028.
High Confidence plans alone could produce 88% full-fibre coverage by January 2029.
Northern Ireland's all-plan projected full-fibre coverage by January 2029 was 99%.
Urban gigabit-capable coverage could rise from 24.2 million homes (93%) to 25.3 million (97%) by January 2029.
Rural gigabit-capable coverage could rise from 2.9 million homes (66%) to 3.7 million (86%) by January 2029.
The report estimates 95% of local authorities could reach at least 85% gigabit-capable residential coverage by January 2029 if all plans are realised.
expansion_rule: For each of 36 contract rows common to December 2025 and July 2026 emit eighteen records: December supplier, December contracted, December built, July supplier continuity, July contracted, July built, contracted delta, built delta, built percentage change, December built ratio, July built ratio, ratio-point change, December unbuilt gap, July unbuilt gap, gap delta, December share of displayed built total, July share of displayed built total, and a long-horizon continuity classification. Append 32 Ofcom Connected Nations and planned-deployment records. Every fifth expanded record is REVALIDATION; all others are UPGRADE.
